question: Which among the following drug is contra-indicated in renal failure?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Pethidine" -> "metabolized to normeperidine" -> "accumulation in renal failure" -> "neurotoxicity risk" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Morphine" -> "metabolized to active metabolites" -> "accumulation in renal failure" -> "increased sedation risk" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Fentanyl" -> "minimal active metabolites" -> "less accumulation in renal failure" -> "safer option" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Atracurium" -> "Hofmann elimination" -> "independent of renal function" -> "safe in renal failure" -> 90%
analysis: In the context of renal failure, the primary concern with drug use is the accumulation of active metabolites that can lead to toxicity. Pethidine is contraindicated in renal failure because it is metabolized to normeperidine, a neurotoxic metabolite that can accumulate in patients with impaired renal function. Morphine also has active metabolites that can accumulate, but it is less contraindicated than pethidine. Fentanyl is considered safer due to minimal active metabolites. Atracurium is safe in renal failure as it is eliminated via Hofmann elimination, independent of renal function. Based on this information, pethidine is the most contraindicated drug in renal failure due to the risk of neurotoxicity from normeperidine accumulation.
